ai.description: Dussumier's Forest Skink reaches 6 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a distinct dark lateral stripe and pale dorsolateral lines. It features a transparent palpebral disc on the lower eyelid.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sphenomorphus dussumieri* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark lateral band that extends from the snout through the eye to the tail.
ai.habitat: Dussumier's Forest Skink inhabits leaf litter in moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: Dussumier's forest skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphenomorphus dussumieri* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Sphenomorphus dussumieri is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu at elevations from sea level to 1,200 meters.
